item.title: No more water conservation efforts needed after feeder water main repair
item.description: The City of Fort St. John has successfully repaired a leak in the feeder water main on February 7th, and conservation efforts no longer needed.

item.title: Hudson’s Hope rescinds ‘boil water’ notice after chlorine concern
item.description: The District of Hudson's Hope says it has resolved water quality concerns after an unexpected error with its chlorine management systems.

item.title: Doctors of BC launches petition to support ‘critical’ RTVS program
item.description: The Doctors of BC petition urges the province to commit to long-term funding for the Real-Time Virtual Support (RTVS) program, which connects rural healthcare professionals with specialist physicians remotely.

item.title: ‘Strategic choice’: B.C. backs bid to host new defence bank in Vancouver
item.description: VICTORIA — British Columbia’s government is supporting a private bid to host a new international bank to finance military projects by democratic nations, with Premier David Eby calling Vancouver the “strategic choice” to host it. item.title: UNBC to offer new nursing pathway for licensed practical nurses
item.description: The University of Northern British Columbia (UNBC) program is designed for practicing licensed practical nurses, and is intended to provide them with a faster route to becoming registered nurses.

item.title: Huskies coach still positive despite series split heading into game three
item.description: The Fort St. John Huskies head coach, Todd Alexander, said it's the "first to three wins" now his team is tied 1-1 with the Fairview Flyers in the first round of the NWJHL playoffs.

item.title: Boxing academy to send foursome to Alberta in search of provincial team slots
item.description: Fivestar Boxing Academy athletes will head to the Western Canadian Boxing Championships in Cochrane, Alberta from February 13th to 15th.

item.title: Community plan shows ‘coordinated, efficient long-term planning,’ First Nation says
item.description: Fort Nelson First Nation held a community engagement meeting about its Reaching For Our Vision (RFOV) plan and Four Pillars Plan in February 2026.

item.title: Kiara Agnew’s family ‘grateful and thankful’ for protest support to demand action on guilty verdict
item.description: Family and supporters of Kiara Agnew protested in Fort St. John on February 8th against the freedom of Ryan Friesen, who was found guilty earlier this year of the Dawson Creek woman's femicide in Mexico in 2023.
